search_log: Searched “The Water Dancer Ta-Nehisi Coates official excerpt first chapter” and opened Penguin’s authorized extract.
Searched “The Water Dancer first person narrator Hiram Walker point of view” and opened explicit structural descriptions and reviews.

Searched the Penguin Random House domain for the title’s excerpt and reading guides; the US product and general reader-guide pages were useful for title verification but did not explicitly describe narrative person.

Searched for narration, multiple narrators, stories within stories, and alternating point of view; the Utah-hosted guide and Ploughshares review consistently describe one controlling first-person narrator, with other characters’ stories embedded locally.
Opened a whole-book LitCharts guide to check interior and ending coverage; it consistently attributes retrospective first-person narration to Hiram and revealed no sustained change of person.
BookRags, GradeSaver, BookBrowse, and search-result snippets also described first-person narration, but they were not needed as cited evidence after stronger opened sources agreed.
person_note: The controlling narrator is Hiram Walker, who retrospectively recounts his own life in the first person. Numerous event quotations independently expose his participating “I,” “my,” and story-specific “we,” while dialogue, aphoristic generic “you,” the Douglass epigraph, and embedded storytelling do not constitute alternate base narration. Penguin’s authorized opening corroborates the first-person voice, and whole-book structural sources identify Hiram as the sole narrator while explicitly treating other characters as storytellers within his narrative. No credible evidence of sustained second- or third-person sections was found; the only material uncertainty is the attribution of the isolated clipped fragment q03595, which does not affect the book-level result.
